newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: National Mutual sees higher yr profit.
newsitem.headline: National Mutual sees higher yr profit.

text.p: Australia's second largest life insurer, National Mutual Holdings Ltd (NMH), said on Tuesday it expected to report a higher profit in the year ending September 30, 1997, based on its first quarter results.

"I am pleased to advise that the results for the first quarter of our current year indicate that, subject to investment markets remaining stable, the profits for 1997 should be greater than the A$210 million achieved in 1996," NMH Chairman Athol Lapthorne told the company's annual meeting.
In discussing the performance of the group's fund management arm, Lapthorne indicated that the bullish investment environment it experienced in 1995/96 was continuing into the current year.

"For a fund manager competitive investment performance is vital and it is pleasing to note that not only did the 1996 overall performance for the majority of our funds show a significant improvement on the prior year, but the start of 1997 has continued this trend."
Lapthorne also said that National Mutual Health Insurance was seeing an improved sales performance after its drop in net profit in 1995/96.

"National Mutual Health took a number of initiatives through the year to improve their situation, including new product launches and improved administration. These changes should start to have an impact on results in 1997," he said.
National Mutual Life, which made a major profit turnaround in 1995/96 to post earnings of A$160 million, was expected to show a further improvement in reducing costs.
"Expenses are being tightly managed. 1996 expenses were reduced by 11 percent, or A$65 million. Further expense reductions are expected in the current year,"
National Mutual Holdings is 51 percent owned by French insurance giant Axa SA.
